transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Gotcha, thanks for sharing that — those intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.  

So when someone calls you after you’ve closed and it hits voicemail… do they usually leave a message, or do you think most of them just move on to the next place?
User: Most don't leave a message, but about 12 calls a week do go to voicemail.
Agent: Mhm, so you’re seeing around 12 after-hours calls a week hit voicemail and most of those people never say who they are.  

When those callers don’t book with you, what do you think typically happens next — do they just call the next place?
User: Yes, most likely they call the next firm when we don't answer right away.
Agent: Right, so those after-hours callers you paid to make the phone ring are basically becoming new cases for the firm down the street.  

Just so I’m clear, are these mostly new-intake calls for potential new matters, or are they a mix of new and existing clients calling in?
User: They are mostly new intake calls for potential new matters.
Agent: Got it, so these are mostly fresh opportunities that never even make it into your system.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what those missed after-hours intake calls are actually costing you in lost cases?
User: No, not exactly. I just know that about 70% would likely book if someone answered.
Agent: Makes sense, and 70% is a strong close rate on real new matters.  

To put some quick numbers on this, what’s a reasonable average value for a new case for you — even on the low end?
User: The average intake value for a new case is about $1,800.
Agent: So with your numbers, those after-hours calls are roughly $65,000 a month in potential new cases slipping to voicemail and then to other firms.  

Given that, it probably makes sense to at least see how we can stop that leak — would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough sometime this week?
User: Yes, I would be interested in a walkthrough to see how your service can help us.
Agent: Nice, that makes sense — it’s a 20‑minute call with Jay, no commitment, just see it in action and then decide.  

To get that set up, what’s your first name?
User: I'm not comfortable sharing personal names. We are 'Bell & Associates Legal'. Let's proceed with booking the live call.
Agent: Totally fine, I hear you — we can just use the firm name.  

And is the number you’re calling from right now the best number to text a confirmation for the walkthrough?
User: No, please use +19172120001 to send the confirmation for the walkthrough.
User: Mm-hmm.
Agent: Alright, so we’ll use that number for the confirmation.  

For the walkthrough with Jay, would you prefer later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would work better for me. What times do you have available?
Agent: Got it, tomorrow works.  

I can get you in tomorrow at either 11:00 or 11:45 Eastern for the 20‑minute walkthrough — which is better for you?
User: 11:45 Eastern works for me. Please book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Bell & Associates Legal — you’re all set for tomorrow at 11:45 Eastern with Jay. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation; you can add it to your calendar or reschedule from that link if something comes up.

Is there anything else I can help you with before we wrap up?

Really glad you called. Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
